notes:
Summary: evaluation for Redwood Dedicated for customer-facing personalization + search and backend inventory QA. Primary ask: throughput guarantees and deterministic latency under peak shopping hours (Black Friday-like spikes).

Key requirements (customer language / shorthand):
- Workloads: high-concurrency personalization requests (~500 qps average expected; peak bursts up to ~2k qps for short windows), search reranking at 200 qps, support-agent chat lower qps but strict p95 latency expectations.
- Latency SLOs: target p95 <= 150ms for personalization paths; p99 under 400ms; search reranking p95 <= 120ms.
- Throughput guarantees: want reserved capacity sizing that covers steady-state + 3x autoscale burst buffer for 10-minute windows.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial ask = equivalent of 16x A100-80GB (or q4_hybrid quantized equivalents) split across 2 regions for redundancy. Customer wants explicit warm standby and cold-warm warmup SLA.
- Reliability / fallback design ask: cross-region failover between us-east and us-west with DNS-based weighted routing + health checks; model-variant fallback policy to smaller quantized models (8-bit int / distilled variant) when primary model saturation detected; automated prefix/KV cache reuse to reduce token compute during failover.
- SLA negotiation points: target uptime 99.9% (customer pushing for 99.95); require 30-min notification for scheduled maintenance, financial credits for >0.1% downtime monthly. Also defined RTO/RPO expectations for lost KV cache (acceptable loss window 2 mins).
- Security/compliance: VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, audit logs retained 1 year, SSO/SAML integration with Okta, data residency restricted to US only.
- Monitoring/ops: need token-level cost breakdowns, per-model latency dashboards, alerts on token-per-second and queue-depth, runbook for cross-region failover (who is on-call).

Recent timeline (bulleted CRM style):
- 2025-09-16: Intro call (Jordan) — high level product fit, customer demo interest.
- 2025-11-05: Infra sizing workshop with SE (Maya) — initial perf numbers, telemetry access requested.
- 2026-01-12: Security intake submitted (SEC-5081 created).
- 2026-02-18: Deep-dive call — reliability + fallback design; recorded (ff_2026-02-18_7b9c2e). Action items: provide sample P95/P99 SLO configs and dedicated capacity pricing.
- 2026-02-25: Send draft SLA + reserved capacity quote (drive link).
- 2026-03-01: Procurement follow-up — asked for formal pricing breakdown and amortized GPU counts per route.

POC scope proposed:
- 2-week benchmark against sample traffic replay covering steady and burst windows (500qps baseline, 2kqps bursts).
- Validate cross-region failover: simulate us-east outage and measure warm-standby spin-up latency and actual p95 under failover.
- Evaluate model-variant fallback: configure primary large model + distilled 8-bit fallback, exercise saturation, verify output quality regressions within threshold.

Technical notes/assumptions for Redwood team (internal):
- Recommend dedicated pool split: 12 GPUs primary in us-east, 4 GPUs warm-standby active in us-west; enable autoscale burst (hot spare capacity) to cover short windows. Consider use of quantized q4_hybrid variant for warm standby to reduce memory pressure.
- Suggest routing policy: latency-first for personalization, cost-limited for background reranking. Implement automatic fallback threshold at 85% capacity or queue depth X.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache with shared cache region replication to reduce token compute during failover.

Customer quotes / color:
- "We need predictable latency during peak. If the model can't respond within the p95 SLA we lose revenue and conversions." — Head of Personalization.
- "Procurement will push back on spend unless we can justify reserved GPU counts vs burst model."

- SE: produce two reserved sizing options (conservative & cost-optimized) with expected p95/p99 numbers and cost per 1M tokens (Maya).
- Security: circulate SOC2 artifacts and schedule follow-up with customer security on 2026-03-10 (Diego).
- Ops: draft failover runbook and alarms; prepare canary traffic script for POC.

- Customer insists on US-only residency which limits cross-region DR options (must remain us-east/us-west only).
